text:
David Vance ran a finger along the faded margin of the old maritime chart, the paper brittle as dried leaves. The map, salvaged from the abandoned Blackwood Bay cannery office, showed depth soundings that no longer matched the shifting seabed. He was looking for discrepancies, for the places where the known world diverged from the official records, a habit born from years of chasing shadows. The scent of salt and decay clung to the room, a familiar companion in this town that always seemed to be holding its breath.

A low, insistent hum began to thrum beneath his feet, a vibration more felt than heard, like the distant churn of some immense, unseen engine. It wasn't the usual Blackwood Bay rumble of the fishing boats or the distant, complaining groan of the old drawbridge. This was deeper, more fundamental, subtly shifting the balance of the air in the room. He felt a fleeting disorientation, a sense that the compass in his gut had spun a full three-sixty. Outside, the familiar squall of gulls seemed to take on a strange, frantic edge, their cries veering wildly as if lost in a clear sky.

David gripped the edge of the desk, steadying himself. The tremor passed, or perhaps simply receded into the background static of the town. But the feeling lingered, a cold premonition that Blackwood Bay wasn't just hiding its secrets, it was actively trying to shake them loose, or perhaps even shake *him* off course. He leaned closer to the chart, his eye catching a penciled note, almost erased, marking a spot far beyond the usual shipping lanes.
